programs.notes: Models on the price list include qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-instruct (EUR 0.20/0.80 per M), llama-3.3-70b-instruct, gpt-oss-120b, gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, mistral-small-3.2. Card requirement not stated. EU data residency.

programs.name: SPAR (Supervised Program for Alignment Research)
programs.amount: Unpaid; approved expenses, compute and API credits covered
programs.notes: Fall 2026 closed; Spring 2027 applications open around December 2026. Part-time, remote, no stipend. Useful for mentorship/credibility, not cash.

programs.name: Heron AI Security Research Fellowship
programs.amount: Unpaid; $1,000+ compute, Claude Code Team accounts, up to $5K conference support per team
programs.notes: Cybersecurity x frontier-AI project fellowship for professionals with 5+ years security experience; autumn cycle closed. Direct topical match (securing AI systems) but no stipend. Express Interest form open for next cycle.

programs.name: Apart Research Fellowships (Apart Fellowship / Partnered Fellowships)
programs.amount: Compute + API credits; stipend not stated
programs.notes: Entry via monthly hackathons; Partnered Fellowships (e.g. Secure Program Synthesis Fellowship with Atlas Computing, Jun-Sep 2026, closed May 31) run remote. New partnered fellowships announced via newsletter.

programs.name: Coefficient Giving: capacity-building on risks from transformative AI
programs.notes: The one Coefficient Giving (ex-Open Phil) AI-risk door that still says apply: training, events, resources, part-time projects; individuals explicitly included. Not a tooling RFP. Direct fetch 403; text from Kagi snippet of the primary page.

programs.name: thanks.dev (dependency-tree payouts)
programs.amount: 0% platform fee, Stripe processing only (secondary); passive
programs.notes: FAQ page 403s; only homepage snippet (maintainers register to be eligible) plus third-party 2026 descriptions read. Payout depends on sponsors who have llm-safe-haven in their npm tree; at current adoption income would be near zero.

programs.name: Coefficient Giving Project Tailwind
programs.amount: Not stated per initiative; founder-scale budgets from a reported USD 20M pool
programs.notes: Call for founders to launch new AI safety organizations. Two-step: express interest, promising candidates invited to submit proposal. Auto-filters submissions not about catastrophic AI risk or that look AI-generated. Primary page returned 403; evidence from Brave snippets of coefficientgiving.org pages incl. a September 2026 update.

programs.name: Halcyon Futures
programs.amount: Career transition grants up to USD 500K; nonprofit seed grants up to USD 1M
programs.notes: Rolling, email-first (hello@halcyonfutures.org). Themes include AI security and cybersecurity. Targets founders launching new orgs or leaders at career inflection points, not project grants.

programs.name: Cloudflare Community Engineers grants
programs.amount: USD 1M pool over two years; per-grant amount not disclosed
programs.notes: Grants for developers building around Cloudflare open-source projects (Astro, Agents SDK, EmDash, Hono, Vinext, workerd, quiche). Applications not yet open. Build-to-fund angle: a security scanner or guardrail layer for Agents SDK / MCP-on-Workers.

programs.name: Cosmos Institute Cosmos Grants
programs.amount: Up to USD 10,000 fast grants, larger for exceptional proposals; 90-day prototype
programs.notes: Tracks: AI for Truth-Seeking, AI and Human Autonomy. Latest round closed Jul 26 2026; interest form for future rounds. Mostly solo builders. Build-to-fund angle: a human-in-control agent guardrail tool under the Autonomy track.

programs.name: OPAQUE AgenTrust Fellowship
programs.amount: USD 30,000 to 50,000 for six months part-time (20 h/week), remote
programs.notes: Inaugural cohort: applications opened Aug 1 and closed early Aug 26 2026 due to volume. Fellows build open standards and code for verifiable AI agents. Strong thematic fit; watch for cohort 2. 20 h/week exceeds the ALG-I 15 h cap.

programs.name: Apart Research sprints (AI Collusion Research Sprint, Oct 23-25 2026)
programs.amount: Cash prizes, typically at least USD 2,000 per sprint
programs.notes: Weekend research hackathons; top teams fast-tracked to Apart Fellowship. Next: AI Collusion Research Sprint Oct 23-25 2026, online. Prize for that sprint not yet listed; prior 2026 sprints stated at least USD 2,000.

programs.name: IBB GründungsBONUS Plus (Berlin)
programs.notes: Open again ('Ab sofort'). Eligible: profit-oriented founders, start-ups, micro-enterprises and Freiberufler with seat in Berlin, founding completed and not older than 18 months at application, seat stays in Berlin 3 years. Reimburses 50% of eligible costs within 2 years, so needs own cash for the other half; taking up a hauptberuflich business ends ALG-I.

programs.name: Digital Commons EDIC (DC-EDIC): 100 Day Challenge + EU Sovereign Tech Fund pilot
programs.geography: EU (DE, FR, NL, IT, LU members; more observers)
programs.notes: Launched Oct 2025, director appointed Mar 2026. First initiatives: a '100 Day Challenge' (select a team, build in the open, ship in 100 days) and a 12-month EU-STF pilot with Germany's Sovereign Tech Agency. No open call, eligibility or amounts yet; scope to be defined in an Implementation Strategy. Watch item.

programs.name: AIXI Labs Research Fellowship
programs.notes: Rolling remote fellowship from a small London non-profit (algorithmic information theory, AIXI-style agent safety). Requires PhD-student-level research background in probability/RL/information theory. Verified via Kagi snippet of the primary page.

programs.name: Subspace Foundation Grants (Autonomys AI3.0)
programs.amount: Unstated; paid in gas credits, $AI3, stablecoins or USD
programs.notes: Five categories (infra, AI dApps, research, community, integration). Stablecoin/USD payout possible. Projects should align with Autonomys Network mission; Google Form application.

programs.name: Open Source Collective fiscal hosting
programs.notes: Requires OSI-style license, repo under an organization (not a personal account) and preferably 2+ admins; a solo maintainer must first move llm-safe-haven to an org. Useful mainly if a grant funder insists on a fiscal host.

programs.name: Open Technology Fund Internet Freedom Fund
programs.notes: Primary page returned 403; homepage snippet confirms support for individuals. Scope is internet freedom / digital-security tools for people under digital authoritarianism, so an agent-security tool only fits if framed for at-risk users. USAGM-funded.

programs.name: Sovereign Tech Resilience (bug/fix bounty + vulnerability management services)
programs.amount: Services (triage, audits, bug bounty via YesWeHack, fix bounty to maintainers); no cash grant to applicant
programs.notes: Rolling applications from critical open digital base technologies (libraries, package managers, protocol implementations, crypto). Only societally relevant, under-supplied technologies. Verified via search snippet of sovereign.tech pages; direct fetch returned 403.

programs.name: Stiftung Mercator (Digitalisierte Gesellschaft)
programs.notes: Rolling two-stage process (sketch by email, ~6 weeks review). Focus areas include 'Digitalisierte Gesellschaft'. Page does not state whether natural persons can apply; foundation favours systemic, longer-term projects with proven expertise, so a solo OSS tool is a long shot.

programs.name: SIDN Fonds Pioneers (NL)
programs.amount: Up to EUR 10,000 (Pioneers, rolling); larger grants only for legal entities via themed calls
programs.geography: Netherlands-focused; impact 'in eerste instantie in Nederland'; residency rule not stated
programs.notes: Natural persons eligible for Pioneers. Results must be shared openly. Whether a Berlin resident can apply is not stated on the page; English page 404.

programs.name: Corrigibility Research Fund (Round 2)
programs.notes: Round 2 deadline Oct 31 2026; apply via Lightcone Commons, applications are public. Round 1 funded 8 grants ($132K total). Research-flavoured: frame tooling as keeping the human principal informed and in control.
